definition: Currah was a British computer peripheral manufacturer, famous mainly for the speech synthesis ROM cartridges it designed for the ZX Spectrum, Commodore 64, and other 8-bit home computers of the 1980s.
details: Currah was a British computer peripheral manufacturer, famous mainly for the speech synthesis ROM cartridges it designed for the ZX Spectrum, Commodore 64, and other 8-bit home computers of the 1980s.

explainer.lead: Currah was a British company that made add-on hardware for home computers. It is best remembered for cartridges that brought speech synthesis to machines such as the ZX Spectrum and Commodore 64 in the 1980s.

tiers.eli5: Currah made extras that people could add to their home computers, a bit like plugging an accessory into a games console. Its best-known accessories helped computers produce speech.
tiers.practitioner: Currah is relevant to engineers studying 1980s computer peripherals, particularly speech synthesis supplied through ROM cartridges. Its products targeted the ZX Spectrum, Commodore 64, and other 8-bit home computers rather than a single host system.
tiers.paperLevel: Currah denotes a British computer peripheral manufacturer, not a synthesis algorithm or model. Its documented contribution is the design of speech-synthesis ROM cartridges for 1980s 8-bit home computers; no particular synthesis method or performance results are specified.

explainer.example: A ZX Spectrum owner could use Currah's speech-synthesis ROM cartridge as an add-on that gave the computer speech-output capability.
